overall_summary: Analysis of 47 unique Shorts reveals a massive performance divergence. First-person cosmic survival scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme exoplanet paradoxes consistently hit the channel's top tier (800-1,050+ views, 20-38 likes, 3-4% engagement rate). Conversely, basic psychology trivia ('fake memories', 'earworms') and recycled animal facts ('three hearts') suffer severe algorithmic fatigue, lingering under 100 views. Videos between 19 and 21 seconds substantially outperform sub-16-second uploads.

winning_patterns.pattern: Second-Person Extreme Planet/Cosmic Hazard Simulation ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet' (1,029 views, 38 likes, 2 comments), 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice' (972 views, 18 likes), and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet' (823 views, 15 likes) drove the highest engagement across the library.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-stakes, sensory-rich 'What If You Fell / Stepped Onto' scenarios with vivid descriptions of physical dissolution and extreme physics.

winning_patterns.pattern: Visual Cosmic Contradictions & Hyper-Specific Astronomical Curiosities
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,029 views, 36 likes) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) generated heavy passive discovery.
winning_patterns.action: Pair a jarring physical paradox with tangible real-world anchors (e.g., darker than coal, day longer than year).

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (multiple iterations yielding 5-53 views, 0 likes) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views, 0 likes) consistently stall at launch.
weak_patterns.action: Halt standalone brain psychology facts unless framed as a high-stakes psychological mystery micro-story.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' was uploaded three separate times (34, 87, 220 views) with diminishing returns; 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' was re-run with flatline metrics.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict fresh-topic filtering to eliminate redundant publishing on identical hooks.

next_video.hook_style: Second-person visceral catastrophe / immediate sensory shock
next_video.concept: What would happen to your body if you got within 1,000 miles of a Magnetar (the strongest magnet in the universe).
next_video.opening_direction: Instant hook visual zooming from the vacuum into a hyper-dense, crackling magnetic core: 'If you drifted within 1,000 miles of a magnetar, you wouldn't crash—your chemistry would simply dissolve.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that long before touching the crust, the 100-billion-tesla field instantly distorts your atoms into microscopic needle shapes, wiping the electrical impulses of your nerves and unraveling your DNA into static dust.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven 'What If You Fell Into / Visited' hook architecture that generated over 1,000 views on exoplanets, but pivots to a completely fresh, unused celestial nightmare (Magnetar SGR 1806-20) to maintain audience novelty and bypass topic fatigue.
fresh_topic_constraints: Do not use diamond planets, burning ice, glass rain, or TrES-2b
Avoid generic space silence or Venus trivia
Keep pacing under 21 seconds with continuous visual escalation

experiment: A/B test the visceral sensory title 'What If You Got Within 1,000 Miles of a Magnetar?' against a mystery-driven question title 'The Space Object That Can Erase Your DNA From 1,000 Miles Away' to gauge whether survival framing or mystery framing yields a higher 24-hour CTR.
